meta.theme: The Trial — guilt without a crime
meta.title: Why Kafka says you were already found guilty

plates.want: Daumier, faceless men of the law (PD)

beats.text: One ordinary morning, a man is arrested. No one will tell him what he has done.
This is Josef K., and this is The Trial — Kafka's nightmare of a court you can never face.
He is allowed to keep his job. He is never shown a charge. Yet the case grinds on.
The deeper he searches for the law, the more corridors and waiting rooms open up.
No one is in charge. Everyone shrugs. The system has no centre — only more system.
Kafka's terror is simple: you may be guilty, condemned, and punished — for nothing you can name.
Ask yourself how much of your life is spent defending a case no one will explain.
